note: The curated core of this repository. Everything else is derived from upstream; this is the part that says which layer answers which question, and -- more usefully -- which layer an agent is about to reach for by mistake. `rejected` is the load-bearing field.

layers.subject: Rustdoc JSON + rustdoc-types
layers.answers: what a crate exposes: modules, signatures, generics, bounds, trait impls, re-exports, attributes, docs
layers.cannot_answer: anything a function does -- there are no bodies in the document at all (RD002); anything about code that is not this crate's public API; anything cfg-gated off at build time (RD005)
layers.needs_build: yes -- rustdoc must compile the crate, or docs.rs must have done so
layers.stability: unstable, nightly-only; format_version has had four breaking bumps in five weeks
layers.reach_for_when: the question is about the shape of a public contract

layers.subject: ra_ap_syntax
layers.answers: exactly how source is written: items, tokens, comments, whitespace, offsets, nesting, and incomplete or invalid code
layers.cannot_answer: what any name refers to; what type anything has; what a macro expands to (SY003)
layers.stability: 0.0.x weekly, but the rowan/AstNode/SyntaxKind design has been stable for years
layers.reach_for_when: the question is about text, formatting, position, or code that does not compile

layers.subject: ra_ap_hir
layers.answers: what names mean: resolution, definitions and references, inferred types, method resolution, trait and impl relationships, macro-expanded semantics, and the mapping back to syntax
layers.cannot_answer: how a body executes as a graph; anything about a project it has not loaded; trivia, which is discarded above the syntax layer
layers.needs_build: a loaded database, and proc macros need building to expand
layers.stability: 0.0.x weekly, every release semver-breaking, no changelog; only 12.84% documented
layers.reach_for_when: the question is what a symbol means or where it resolves to

layers.subject: ra_ap_load-cargo + ra_ap_project_model
layers.answers: how a real Cargo project becomes an analysis database: workspace discovery, the crate graph, roots, dependencies, sysroot, the selected configuration
layers.cannot_answer: any fact about code -- it makes the other layers able to answer, and answers nothing itself
layers.needs_build: yes -- build scripts and proc macros are compiled unless disabled
layers.needs_network: yes, unless dependencies are already fetched
layers.stability: 0.0.x weekly, and explicitly NOT an API boundary upstream, so the most volatile of the three
layers.reach_for_when: you need hir or syntax to see a real crate rather than a loose file

layers.subject: MIR via rustc_driver + rustc_middle::mir
layers.obtained_by: rustc -Zunpretty=mir, -Zdump-mir; or rustc_public for a typed API
layers.answers: how a body executes: basic blocks, terminators, locals, places, operands, rvalues, calls, branches, drops, moves
layers.cannot_answer: what the source looked like; original variable names, which survive only as debug annotations (XL002); anything about items with no body
layers.stability: unstable and unversioned; the textual view says it is for human consumers only (MI006)
layers.reach_for_when: the question is about control flow, drops, or what actually runs

layers.subject: rustc_mir_dataflow
layers.obtained_by: rustc -Zdump-mir-dataflow=yes, or the Analysis trait inside the compiler
layers.answers: how state evolves along execution paths: initialisation, liveness, borrows, moves, and any custom forward or backward analysis
layers.cannot_answer: anything MIR itself does not already carry -- it derives facts over the graph, it does not add to it
layers.stability: unstable; roughly ten signature-affecting commits a year, and one reversal
layers.reach_for_when: the question is whether something holds at a program point, not merely which edges exist

layers.subject: cargo metadata / cargo_metadata
layers.answers: package identity, targets, workspace structure, dependency identities and renames, the resolved graph, manifest metadata, declared features
layers.cannot_answer: anything whatsoever about code; which features a particular build resolved, as opposed to which are declared (PL003)
layers.needs_build: no -- resolution only, and --no-deps skips even that
layers.needs_network: yes unless the lockfile is complete and the registry cached
layers.stability: the wire format has been version 1 since ~2017; the crate that parses it is pre-1.0
layers.reach_for_when: the question is about packages, targets, features or dependency identity

questions.question: What does this crate expose publicly?
rejected: sees every item whether public or not, and has no notion of the documented surface
knows the package, not a single item inside it

questions.question: What is the exact signature, generics and bounds of an item?
rejected: has the signature as written, but not the resolved paths in it

questions.question: Is this item deprecated, or gated behind a feature?
rejected: for the feature half: a gated-off item is absent entirely, with no record that it exists

questions.question: What does this function do?
rejected: contains no function bodies at all -- the single most common wrong turn
has the body as text with nothing resolved

questions.question: What type does this expression have?
rejected: records the type as written and infers nothing
has types, but the expression structure is gone

questions.question: Where is this symbol defined, and where is it used?
rejected: can find the spelling but cannot tell two different items with the same name apart

questions.question: Which impl does this method call resolve to?
rejected: lists impls but cannot resolve a call site
sees a method name and nothing else

questions.question: What traits does this type implement?
rejected: also answers, and is the right choice when the type is local or private rather than a published API

questions.question: What does this macro expand to?
rejected: holds the invocation unexpanded -- MACRO_CALL is as far as it goes

questions.question: Where exactly is this in the file, including comments and whitespace?
rejected: keeps spans but not the text between them

questions.question: How do I analyse code that does not compile?
How do I rewrite every occurrence of a pattern?
rejected: can match structurally but will not check that the replacement resolves

questions.question: Which branch runs, and under what condition?
rejected: has the expression tree, not the graph

questions.question: Where is this value dropped?
rejected: drops appear nowhere in the source
knows ownership but not drop placement

questions.question: Is this local initialised at this point?
rejected: gives the graph; whether a fact holds along every path is a fixpoint over it

questions.question: Is this local live here?
rejected: the same reason: liveness is derived over the graph, not recorded in it

questions.question: How do I write my own dataflow analysis?
rejected: if you remember AnalysisDomain or GenKillAnalysis: both are gone, merged into Analysis and removed respectively

questions.question: What are the call edges out of this function?
rejected: has no call graph of any kind
can resolve a call it is shown, but does not enumerate a body's calls as a graph

questions.question: What is the crate graph and which features are on?
rejected: with --no-deps the resolve field is null, which is not the same as no dependencies
builds its own graph for analysis, which is not the Cargo view

questions.question: How do I load a real Cargo project into an analysis database?
rejected: operates on a database; it does not create one
describes the project without loading anything

questions.question: Which MIR am I looking at -- before or after optimisation?
rejected: asking for 'the MIR' is ambiguous: built, analysis and runtime differ

questions.question: Which rustdoc format version am I parsing?
rejected: the toolchain's own version does not tell you: docs.rs serves whatever its fleet built, and rustdoc-types 0.61.0 is itself served at format 60

questions.question: Can I cache a rustdoc Id and use it later?
rejected: no: an Id is a position in one document. Adding an unrelated item shifts it

questions.question: Why is this item missing from the documentation I generated?
rejected: three different causes look identical: not public, cfg-gated off, or in a private module

questions.question: What node kinds can appear in a Rust syntax tree?
rejected: documents the types, not the grammar they encode

questions.question: Which rust-analyzer version am I actually running?
rejected: the binary reports a rustc release number; there is no published mapping to an ra_ap crate version

questions.question: Can I script these tools and trust the exit code?
rejected: sometimes: ssr exits 1 on a refused rule, but parse exits 0 on source it could not parse

questions.question: Which layer should I use at all?

views.shows: HIR with inferred types written in
typed HIR, flattened and fully typed
the control-flow graph: blocks, terminators, locals

oracles.subject: rustc
oracles.question: which compiler is this?
oracles.answers_for: the compiler that will produce every MIR and dataflow observation
oracles.trap: a bare +nightly floats; use a dated toolchain

oracles.subject: rustdoc
oracles.question: which format version does this toolchain emit?
oracles.trap: says nothing about what docs.rs will serve for a crate

oracles.subject: rustdoc JSON
oracles.question: which format version is THIS document?
oracles.command: read the format_version field of the payload
oracles.trap: the only reliable reading. rustdoc-types 0.61.0, which defines FORMAT_VERSION = 61, is served by docs.rs at format 60

oracles.subject: rustdoc-types
oracles.question: which format version does this crate model?
oracles.trap: the minor version equals the format version, so 0.61.0 means 61

oracles.subject: rust-analyzer
oracles.question: which rust-analyzer is this?
oracles.answers_for: the rustc release the binary was built in
oracles.trap: NOT an ra_ap_* crate version, and there is no published mapping between them. The rust-analyzer repository carries no version number at all

oracles.subject: ra_ap_* crates
oracles.question: which release is this?
oracles.trap: 0.0.N is bumped weekly and every release is semver-breaking; a caret requirement will float across breaking changes

oracles.subject: cargo
oracles.question: which metadata schema is this?
oracles.trap: version has read 1 for years while new keys were added; tolerate unknown fields

oracles.subject: cargo_metadata
oracles.question: which parser version is this?
oracles.trap: pre-1.0, so a minor bump is breaking; it may also lag fields Cargo already emits

unreachable.capability: rustdoc JSON for any rustc-internal crate
unreachable.why: the rust-docs-json rustup component ships std, core, alloc, proc_macro, test and std_detect only
unreachable.instead: the rustc-docs component, or the pinned source in content/corpus/rustc

unreachable.why: still requires a nightly compiler and rustc_private
unreachable.instead: rustc -Zunpretty=stable-mir to see the projection, or the pinned rustc_public source

unreachable.why: panics on this build with 'Try to use attached db, but not db is attached'
unreachable.instead: ssr with a rule, or ast-grep for a purely structural match

unreachable.capability: a JSON Schema for cargo metadata output
unreachable.why: rust-lang/cargo publishes no schema file for the metadata envelope
unreachable.instead: the Cargo book page in content/corpus/cargo, and cargo_metadata's own types

unreachable.capability: a mapping from an ra_ap version to a rust-analyzer commit
unreachable.why: versions are minted at publish time by xtask; the repository has no version field
unreachable.instead: match by publication date, and record that it is an inference

unreachable.why: an item gated off is absent from the document with no trace
unreachable.instead: the [features] table of Cargo.toml, indexed as features.tsv

unreachable.why: the format models the documented surface, not code
unreachable.instead: MIR, THIR or the HIR layer

unreachable.why: rustdoc moved to a search.index/ stringdex backend; the old path is a 404
unreachable.instead: search.index/root.js, crates.js, or each crate's all.html
